instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: PFA Team of the Year after a broken leg cost him most of 1995/96; eight assists from left-back and the best left-foot delivery in the division that season.
Two divisions and two seasons on from Liverpool; at 31 a steady, well-delivered left-back for a newly promoted side rather than the PFA pick of 1996/97.
Thirty-three and the best player in a mid-table Spurs side; the late runs and the finishing were intact, the legs less so.
Eleven assists and an England cap; elite delivery, nothing else above the standard.
Two seasons outside the top flight in between; at 34 a squad left-sided player whose delivery was still the only part of his game above the level.
Twelve league goals from 859 minutes, mostly from the bench. Rated on finishing ability, not on the limited starting role behind Yorke and Cole.
Seventeen league goals from 23 starts, his best return over a full season; finishing of a genuinely elite standard even while rotated.
Used wide and off the bench before the knee trouble that ended his career took hold; no league goals, but the fall is one of role and fitness rather than ability.
Ever-present and the metronome of an Ipswich side that finished fifth; genuinely good at the unglamorous parts, never near elite.
Nineteen, but already an Ireland international with outstanding technique and twelve goals for a lower-half side; the rating is for what he could do, not for the fee Inter paid.
Three league goals in a season spent largely behind Viduka and Fowler; the ability was unchanged from Coventry, the opportunity was not.
Two lost seasons at Leeds and abroad in between; at 28 a fringe player for a promoted side, not the England winger of 1994.
Six starts for a Bradford side relegated with 26 points; at 29 he was finished as a top-flight footballer.
Eleven assists from wide after two seasons out of the side; Wimbledon’s set-piece taker.
Twenty, and already one of the quickest and most technically able midfielders in the division.
Fifteen starts - the hamstring trouble that shaped his career; rated on the player when fit, which was unchanged.
Thirty-three starts in a Newcastle side that finished third, and England’s first-choice right-sided midfielder; his most complete season.
The attacking left-back of the side that led the title race by twelve points; genuinely good going forward, regularly exposed defending.
Thirty-five and a third-choice keeper covering three games; still competent, well short of the Newcastle regular of the mid-1990s.
Twelve league goals from the right in a Double season and the Football Writers’ pick; elite, and the equal of his Invincibles year rather than a peak above it.
Four seasons of development on from 1999/00: by the Invincibles year he was an elite wide forward, timing runs beyond the front line rather than holding the touchline.
His one season as a first-choice centre-half in a title-winning side; a good defender rather than the liability he is remembered as.
Ten starts for a Leicester side relegated with 28 points; two seasons on from Derby and past his best.
A back injury ended his career at 28; five starts and no real football after them.
The last full season before the illness that ended his career at 31; still a competent Premier League centre-half here.
Twenty at the start of the Double season and first choice for it; the athleticism and the recovery pace were already exceptional, the defensive detail still coming.
The best left-back in the league at 22 and England’s first choice.
Ruptured cruciate ligament in the third game; he never played regular top-flight football again.
A season on from the cruciate rupture and visibly not the player of 1998/99; twelve starts, and then out of the top flight for good.
Ever-present at 23 and, on reading of the game and recovery pace, close to the best defender in the division; the knee that later limited him had not yet done so.
A composed, left-footed ball-playing centre-half in a relegated side; the move to Celtic and a long Everton career reflect the ability on show here.
Six years on from Bolton - Celtic, and a testicular cancer diagnosis and recovery, in between; the same composed left-footed defender, a little more experienced and a little slower.
A central defender in an Everton side that finished fourth conceding 46; solid and well organised rather than newly elite.
A regular in a Sunderland side relegated with 19 points, the lowest total in the division’s history at the time; evidence about the side more than the player.
Fifteen goals and eight assists at 22; strong, aggressive and a better footballer than the caricature. His peak season.
Twelve starts and six goals for a relegated Coventry before his knee gave out; the physical game was already blunted.
The right-sided supply line for the Quinn/Phillips partnership; the delivery was essentially the whole game.
Twenty-two goals for a promoted side that finished third; pace, power, finishing and genuine creation.
The decline from here is real and well documented — depression, loss of form, loss of the physical edge — rather than a run of bad luck.
Five starts, then retirement at 29; the athleticism and confidence that made him an 85 in 1995/96 were gone entirely.
A World Cup winner in a Chelsea side that conceded 30; rated at the Pallister anchor — good, occasionally elite, and error-prone.
Thirty-two, and a season away from Marseille; the passing was undimmed, the pace that covered for his risk-taking was not.
Thirty-three starts as first-choice centre-half in a Newcastle side that finished fourth; his best season.
Seventeen league goals and a Champions League semi-final; a genuinely complete centre-forward - touch, strength, finishing - a rung below elite for consistency rather than quality.
Twenty league goals in a Leeds side that finished fifteenth and was being dismantled around him.
Twenty-eight and restricted to fifteen starts in his first Middlesbrough season; the Achilles trouble that dogged him had begun.
Thirty, and a back-up at Sunderland after relegation with Derby; four starts.
Twenty, and already Chelsea’s best defender across a full season; the positional reading and the aerial dominance were finished products long before the rest of his game.

PFA Player of the Year in a title-winning side that conceded fifteen league goals. World class - reading, organisation and front-foot defending all at their peak, and the equal of the Ferdinand 2007/08 anchor.
Two seasons on from the teenager of 1998/99 and three years older; the dribbling had become a genuine Premier League weapon.
Thirty-five, three starts, and three seasons after his last regular top-flight football; a passing midfielder with nothing left physically.
Two seasons in Spain in between; back at City at 27 as a twelve-start squad forward, the awkward brilliance intact and the sharpness gone.
Ten league goals from left-back, most of them penalties; a fearsome left foot and a genuinely hard defender, with obvious discipline and mobility limits.
The knee finally gave out; nine starts and retirement at 30.
